situation.summary: Tenant Elowen Marr reported misted kitchen glazing, water around the frame, a cold kitchen and damp concern, with pets at the property (E001, S:initial-request). The landlord, Orren Vale, approved the glass replacement only conditionally: he was happy if the total was £180 (E010). The agency relayed £150 plus VAT (E011), and the contractor, Clearfirth Glazing, ordered glass (E018). No visit has been booked or recorded, and on 2 September the contractor said the glass had not arrived and gave no delivery date (E021). On 10 September an invoice dated that day for "supply and fit 1 pane" was uploaded with no amount and no visit evidence (E023, A1), and the agency filed it to the record (E024). The next move is with the contractor, to confirm the glass and fitting dates, what the invoice covers and its amount, before anything is paid or the landlord is told it is complete.
situation.task: Establish with the contractor whether the glass has arrived, when fitting can happen, what invoice NBL-013-INV-09 covers and its amount, and whether the water and cold concern was assessed. Recommended next action: contractor.chase by email to Sella Vane (Clearfirth Glazing), with the draft in the openAsks entry, plus a tenant.update to Elowen Marr in the same turn.

decision.actionLabel: Chase Clearfirth Glazing to confirm whether the kitchen pane has been fitted, and ask for invoice NBL-013-INV-09 again with the amount, VAT basis and completion photos
decision.message:
Subject: 8 Brackenmere Walk, Vellumbrook, ZZ1 1ZZ: kitchen glazing, invoice NBL-013-INV-09

Hello Sella,

Thank you for invoice NBL-013-INV-09, dated 10 September 2025, for "Supply and fit 1 pane of glass to the kitchen glazing". Before we can pass it to the landlord, we need a few things from you:

1. Confirmation that the work is done. When we spoke on 2 September, the glass had not arrived and no appointment had been made. We have no record of a visit since then. Please tell us the date you fitted the pane. If it has not been fitted yet, please tell us when the glass is due and suggest some fitting dates. The tenant wants to be there, so we will check any dates with her before you attend.
2. A complete copy of the invoice as a PDF. The copy we have shows no amount. Please give the amount excluding VAT, the VAT and the total, and tell us whether Clearfirth Glazing is VAT-registered. The landlord approved £150 plus VAT (£180 in total). Any figure above that needs his approval before it can be paid.
3. Before and after photos of the kitchen glazing, plus a note if you saw anything at the frame that could explain the water the tenant reported collecting there.

Please reply by Friday 12 September 2025. We will hold the invoice until then. If we have not heard from you, we will phone you on Monday 15 September.

Kind regards,
Tamsin Rook
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: An invoice for "supply and fit" was uploaded on 10 September (E023, A1), but it has no amount. The last contractor update (E021, 2 September) said the glass had not arrived and no appointment was made. No visit is recorded since then, and the 9 September note (E022) is not evidence that one took place. Under the manual, an invoice with no readable amount and no completion evidence cannot go to the landlord, and invoices must be checked against what was approved. The landlord approved £150 plus VAT, total £180 (E010, E011). The only party who can confirm whether the work was done and give the amount and VAT basis is the contractor. It is not safe to close the case or update the landlord yet. Approval is already on record, so the landlord does not need to be asked for anything now. The tenant can independently confirm whether the pane was fitted. She was last told the agency would be in touch when the glass arrived (E019), so she should be asked in the same turn.
decision.expectedOutcome: The contractor confirms the fitting date and sends a full PDF invoice with the VAT basis and photos, or confirms the work is still pending and suggests dates. The tenant confirms whether the pane has been replaced and whether the misting and water have stopped.
boundaries: An uploaded invoice does not prove the pane was fitted.
This chase does not approve or pay the invoice, or approve any amount above £150 plus VAT (£180 total).
The contractor's word alone is not completion evidence. The tenant's confirmation is also needed.
This does not assess or settle the tenant's wider concerns about damp, cold or water at the frame.
remainingWork: Once completion is evidenced and the invoice is checked against £180, update the landlord with the invoice and how it will be paid.
If the invoice is above £180 or VAT is charged differently, take the difference to the landlord before paying.
If water at the frame or damp continues after the glass is replaced, raise it with the landlord as a separate scope decision.
Close the case once the tenant confirms the fix, the landlord has been told and the invoice is settled.
assumptions: The landlord's approval of £150 plus VAT, £180 in total, is treated as given (E010 together with E011).
No visit has been recorded since 2 September. The work may have been done without the agency's knowledge.

alternatives.whyNot: The invoice has no amount, and there is no evidence the work was done.
Completion is not evidenced, the landlord has not been told and the invoice is not settled.
The playbook covers this: ask for a readable invoice and completion evidence. No safety risk, dispute or overrun has been confirmed yet.

The contractor holds all of these facts, so this is a chase to the contractor. The only proof of fitting would be the contractor's own invoice. problems.issue: c1 [evidence] The message thanks the contractor for the invoice, but the record only shows Tamsin uploading it (E023). It doesn't show who sent it or when. (E023, E024, A1). Fix: Say 'the invoice copy on our file' instead of 'thank you for the invoice you sent'.

c2 [scope] The request for a note on 'anything at the frame that could explain the water' goes beyond the approved scope. The next step doesn't need it, and the wider damp concern is a separate decision for the landlord. (E005, E008). Fix: Drop that sentence, or keep only the request for before and after photos.

The system note calls it approved (E012). Stating 'approved £150 plus VAT (£180 total)' is reasonable but leans on this. (E010, E011, E012). Fix: No change needed. Keep the message as 'approved up to £180 in total', and check the invoice total against that figure before forwarding.

c4 [timing] The automatic no-early-chase flag is a false positive. It cites the proposal's own reply-by date, not a date the contractor promised. The contractor's last promise was an update when the glass arrived (E021). The new invoice is a new open point, not a repeat ask, so this chase is not premature. (E021, E023). Fix: Proceed. The phone follow-up on Monday 15 September is fine because it is after the stated reply-by date.

c1 [communication] The contractor message asks her to note anything at the frame that could explain the tenant's water. That is not needed to settle the invoice or the completion evidence. It also drifts into the wider damp concern, which the plan itself treats as a separate scope decision. (E005, E023). Fix: Drop the frame-observation request from point 3, or keep it only as an optional line. Keep the ask for before and after photos.

The landlord, Orren Vale, approved the glass replacement only conditionally: he was happy if the total was £180 (E010). Done so far:
- E016: 14 Aug: call with contractor, who is at a funeral; no attendance time agreed.

responses.evidence: The contractor never promised anything by Friday 12 September 2025. That date comes from our own colleague's draft, and the situation file marks it "(proposed; not yet sent)". It is the reply-by date we would set, not a date the contractor gave. Her only commitments on record have no date. On 24 August (E018) she said the glass was ordered, with no arrival or visit estimate. On 2 September (E021) she said she "could not estimate delivery because of supplier delays" and "would provide an update when it arrived". So there is no promised date that has not yet passed. This is also not a repeat chase sent too soon. Our last written ask was on 27 August (E020) and our last call was on 2 September (E021), 8 days before the decision moment. More importantly, a new fact has arrived. On 10 September an invoice for "Supply and fit 1 pane of glass" was uploaded with no amount (E023, A1), but the record shows no visit and, as of 2 September, no glass. Refinement 4 says a new open point is asked about now, not held back by the early-chase rule. Domain manual 0a.3 says to ask the sender for a readable invoice rather than rely on or forward one with no amount. Rule 0a.4 says to check an invoice against the approved figure before forwarding it. Waiting would leave an invoice that conflicts with the record and has no amount sitting on file. The plan is unchanged.

revision.message:
Subject: 8 Brackenmere Walk, Vellumbrook, ZZ1 1ZZ: kitchen glazing, invoice NBL-013-INV-09

Hello Sella,

Thank you for invoice NBL-013-INV-09, dated 10 September 2025, for "Supply and fit 1 pane of glass to the kitchen glazing". Before we can pass it to the landlord, we need a few things from you:

1. Confirmation that the work is done. When we spoke on 2 September, the glass had not arrived and no appointment had been made. We have no record of a visit since then. Please tell us the date you fitted the pane. If it has not been fitted yet, please tell us when the glass is due and suggest some fitting dates. The tenant wants to be there, so we will check any dates with her before you attend.
2. A complete copy of the invoice as a PDF. The copy we have shows no amount. Please give the amount excluding VAT, the VAT and the total, and tell us whether Clearfirth Glazing is VAT-registered. The landlord approved £150 plus VAT (£180 in total). Any figure above that needs his approval before it can be paid.
3. Before and after photos of the kitchen glazing, plus a note if you saw anything at the frame that could explain the water the tenant reported collecting there.

Please reply by Friday 12 September 2025. We will hold the invoice until then. If we have not heard from you, we will phone you on Monday 15 September.

Kind regards,
Tamsin Rook
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
revision.rationale: An invoice for "supply and fit" was uploaded on 10 September (E023, A1), but it has no amount. The contractor's last update (E021, 2 September) said the glass had not arrived, gave no delivery date and made no appointment. No visit is recorded since then. The 9 September note (E022) does not show that one took place. The contractor gave no date for her next update, so there is no promised date to wait for. The invoice is a new question to put to her now. The manual says an invoice with no readable amount and no completion evidence cannot go to the landlord, and that invoices must be checked against what was approved. The landlord approved £150 plus VAT, £180 in total (E010, E011). Only the contractor can confirm whether the work was done and give the amount and VAT basis. Approval is already on record, so the landlord does not need to be asked for anything now. The tenant can confirm independently whether the pane was fitted. She was last told we would be in touch when the glass arrived (E019), so she is asked in the same turn.
revision.expectedOutcome: The contractor confirms the fitting date and sends a full PDF invoice with the VAT basis and photos, or confirms the work is still pending and suggests dates. The tenant confirms whether the pane has been replaced and whether the misting and water have stopped.
